properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 17 at 10:07AM EDT until September 22 at 10:34AM EDT by NWS Northern Indiana
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Indiana...

Wabash River near Bluffton IN affecting Wells County.

Wabash River near Linn Grove affecting Wells and Adams Counties.

For the Wabash River...including Linn Grove, Bluffton IN, Wabash,
Logansport...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Wabash River near Bluffton IN.

* WHEN...Until Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, The outlying portion of West Washington
Street becomes impassible and SR 116 west of Bluffton begins to
flood.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:45 AM EDT Thursday the stage was 14.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 8.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:45 AM EDT Thursday was 14.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 15.6 feet
just after midnight tonight. It will then fall below flood stage
late Monday morning.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Detailed river forecasts and additional information can be found at
www.weather.gov/iwx under Rivers and Lakes.

This statement will be updated within the next 12 to 24 hours.

properties.description:

* WHERE...Northwestern Auglaize County in west central Ohio...
Mercer County in west central Ohio...
Northwestern Shelby County in west central Ohio...

* WHEN...Until 445 PM EDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

Mendon, Chickasaw, Montezuma, Tama, Neptune, Carthagena,

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 17 at 10:01AM EDT until September 17 at 2:15PM EDT by NWS Northern Indiana
properties.description:
At 1001 AM EDT, Radar indicates that between 2 and 5 inches of rain
have fallen since last night.  Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to
2 inches are possible in the warned area as heavier showers and
thunderstorms move in from the west.  Flash flooding is already
occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Huntington, Bluffton, Decatur, Berne, Ossian, Geneva, Andrews,
Markle, Monroe, Lancaster, Preble, Nottingham, Zanesville,
Willshire, Uniondale, Wren, Poneto, Vera Cruz, Murray and North
Oaks.

properties.areaDesc: Citrus, FL; Levy, FL; Marion, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 17 at 10:44AM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Levy, Marion and Citrus
Counties.

.The Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon (US 41) has been steadily
rising since July and on September 15, reached flood stage. The cause
of the high water along the Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon is
excessive hydrilla growth (from river bottom to the water surface)
along a 4.5 mile stretch of river between US 41 and Lake Rousseau.
The hydrilla is acting like a dam and holding water back, causing
water levels to rise.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:45 AM EDT Thursday the stage was 28.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:45 AM EDT Thursday was 28.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 28.2 feet.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.3
feet on 10/05/1965.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at midnight EDT.
